elements.content: This hole is nine problems away from a fallout shelter.
But fallout is radioactive dust, and it falls straight in. So we add a roof.
But a thin roof barely stops radiation. So we pile three feet of packed dirt on top.
But dirt is heavy, and the roof starts to sag. So we brace it with thick timber beams.
But now there's no way in. So we dig an entrance that turns a sharp corner. Radiation hates corners. Preppers call it a baffle entry.
But sealed underground, the air goes stale fast. So we add a hand-cranked fan and a filtered vent pipe.
But you'll be down here a while. So we stock water: one gallon per person, per day.
But what goes in must come out. So we add a lidded bucket toilet and plenty of bags.
But it's pitch black. So we hang battery lanterns. Not candles, they eat your air.
But you can't hear the outside world. So we add a hand-crank radio. That's why the official advice is: get inside, stay inside, stay tuned.
And here's the surprise: fallout fades fast. After seven hours, it's ten times weaker. After two days, a hundred times.
Illustration only. Not engineering advice. Check local codes and official guidance at ready.gov.
Nine problems. Nine fixes. One hole, ready for two weeks.
